constraints: No edits to application, tests, or dataset

findings.title: Five-decimal intermediate arithmetic tolerance hides amplified errors
findings.reproduction: Claim 1/1000000=0.000002, then multiply claimed result by 1000000 to get 2. Reference result is 1. Evaluator returns process=correct, answer_correct=false, reference_equivalent=true, first_error=null.
findings.recommendation: Separate official final-answer scoring from high-precision local arithmetic checking. Preserve uncertainty if supported rounding cannot be distinguished from an error; do not let symbolic equivalence erase numeric inconsistency. Add regression case and rescore saved traces.

findings.title: Percent normalization changes official five-decimal answer tolerance
findings.reproduction: RCL/2016/page_37.pdf-2 gold is 98.18 with percent unit. Candidate final=98.1801 percent is scored answer_correct=true, although official source-scale comparison round(98.1801,5)==round(98.18,5) is false.
findings.recommendation: Convert candidate value to the reference answer's original numeric scale before applying official comparison. Keep normalized value as a display/semantic field.

findings.title: Contradictory judge output can receive false error-type credit
findings.reproduction: Mocked judge returns process=correct, first_error_step=null, error_type=formula and is accepted. For a formula-error label, metrics then report detection=0/1 but error_type=1/1.
findings.recommendation: Validate error-type enum and require both error fields null for correct/uncertain verdicts. Also require predicted process=incorrect in the error-type numerator, independently of protocol validation.

remaining_precision_caveat: Prompt precision and local tolerance differ in theoretical cases, but all 30 generated traces have zero arithmetic or answer-consistency hard findings, so no observed rounding false positives in this batch.
